inlines.v: RETORT', verb transitive [Latin retortus, retorqueo; re and torqueo, to throw.] 1. To throw back; to reverberate. And they retort that beat again to the first giver. 2. To return an argument, accusation, censure or incivility; as, to retort the charge of vanity. He pass'd through hostile scorn; and with retorted scorn, his back he turn'd. 3. To bend or curve back; as a retorted line. RETORT', verb intransitive To return an argument or charge; to make a severe reply. He retorted upon his adversary with severity. RETORT', noun 1. The return of an argument, charge or incivility in reply; as the retort courteous. 2. In chimistry, a spherical vessel with its neck bent, to which the receiver is fitted; used in distillation.
